claims.text: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is essential for reliable and trustworthy machine learning.
Recent multi-modal OOD detection neglects the rich contextual information of ID classes.
Indiscriminately using LLM world knowledge causes catastrophic damage to OOD detection due to LLM hallucinations.
Selective generation from LLMs enhances OOD detection performance.
The proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-modal OOD detection baselines.

evidence.description: Indiscriminately using such knowledge causes catastrophic damage to OOD detection due to LLMs' hallucinations, as is observed by our analysis.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art.

methodologies.name: Selective Generation OOD Detection with LLMs
methodologies.description: A framework that applies world knowledge to enhance OOD detection via selective generation using consistency-based uncertainty calibration and visual object extraction from images.

limitations.text: Recent multi-modal OOD detection leverages textual information from ID class names but neglects rich contextual information.
Indiscriminate use of LLM knowledge degrades OOD detection performance due to hallucinations.
